entries.body:
## Explanation: conditions belong in the story

A pile of ingredients does not explain why a new organization forms. Arrangement, energy flow and surroundings matter. The supplied world explanation uses a star: a gravitationally organized body establishes pressure, temperature and reaction conditions that were unavailable to the earlier diffuse gas. The later availability of heavier elements expands the kinds of chemistry that can occur. This is the source's explanatory example, not a calculation performed for this article. See [the world explanation](/documents/world-explanation/) and [the star example](/examples/star/).

The useful distinction is between having components and being able to combine them under particular conditions. A structure may alter those conditions. It can supply boundaries, concentrate material or maintain an environment in which a later structure can persist. The world explanation's retained background addendum describes this as a changing landscape of reachable possibilities. A possible configuration need not already exist as a finished object awaiting discovery.

The same reasoning helps explain why the surroundings cannot be removed from the story of life. Suitable chemistry and a maintained environment are enabling conditions; they do not guarantee the historical path to a cell. [Life and its environment](/examples/life-environment/) keeps that unresolved route visible. These examples use different mechanisms. Their similarity is an explanatory pattern, not evidence that every scale shares an identical equation.

## Proposal: recursive formation and changed surroundings

The locked core permits compatible, internally active lower-level units to form a collective organization. The units can differ and need not copy themselves first. The resulting whole introduces collective constraints and modes while its parts remain active. The registered meanings are :claim[UT-D06] and :claim[UT-D08]; this article adds no definition.

RRG asks whether persistent organization can serve both as a reusable unit and as a contributor to the environment for further organization. That question is stronger than observing familiar cases. To test it, a particular model must say which conditions change, which new formations become reachable and what would count as failure. [The framework](/framework/) and [the mathematical programme](/math/) describe candidate ways to make such questions precise. They remain a research programme.

The effective-interaction extension adds another conditional possibility: lower-level organization may support an effective interaction channel relevant to a higher organization. The [evidence catalogue](/evidence/catalogue/) reports distinct physical cases under supplied conditions. It does not establish fundamental-force unification or a universal quantitative law. The conjecture :claim[UT-C01] keeps that distinction explicit.

## Actual results: what is available here

This article reports no new experiment, simulation or derivation. The [claim coverage](/research-status/claims/) records open boundaries; [evidence catalogue](/evidence/catalogue/) retains the original access and inspection limits. Existing reported support can motivate a question without proving its universal extension.

Historical cavity and response calculations were not selected or run for this website. A new result would require a named model, assumptions, inputs, procedure, outputs and limits, rather than an arrow added to the explanation. The current [open questions](/open-problems/) are the place to see what remains unresolved.

The practical reading question is therefore: which existing organization changes which conditions, and what later formation becomes possible under those conditions? Answering it in a concrete system would be progress; the pattern alone is a proposal.

entries.body:
## Explanation: a useful description depends on the question

A molecule contains atoms with internal activity, yet a description at another scale can treat the molecule as a participant in a reaction or as a rotating object. That useful simplification does not erase the atoms. It selects the collective properties relevant to an interaction. The supplied [world explanation](/documents/world-explanation/) discusses this packaging of complexity, and the [molecule example](/examples/molecule/) illustrates how collective constraints coexist with active parts.

A whole is not automatically a useful unit just because we can draw a boundary around it. The question is whether the organization persists in the circumstances of interest and supports a collective response that the next description can use. A description useful for one timescale or perturbation can be inadequate for another. When a molecule dissociates, continuing to treat it as the same intact participant would hide a material change.

RRG's geometry includes relations, connectivity, boundaries and constraints, as well as arrangement. Its mode structure includes phase, amplitude, coupling, propagation and characteristic times. One frequency number cannot stand in for all of that organization. The [string example](/examples/string/) makes the limitation concrete: supported patterns depend on boundaries, tension and mass per unit length. A standing-wave analogy is not itself proof of a self-maintaining higher-level object.

## Proposal: collective organization becomes reusable

The registered resonant geometry is :claim[UT-D03]. The locked stability meaning, :claim[UT-D04], concerns a self-consistent geometry–mode organization. It does not mean permanence. Lifetimes and perturbation recovery are system-specific measurements of this meaning, rather than replacement definitions.

::claim{id="UT-D05" view="plainLanguage"}

This scale definition anchors the useful-unit question. In higher-level formation (:claim[UT-D06]), parts can be different, retain internal activity and play different roles. Their collective organization can then participate in another combination. The structural recursion (:claim[UT-D08]) does not require identical microscopic mechanisms at every step or a perfectly regular ladder of sizes and times.

To assess a candidate whole, a model needs to specify what counts as its organization, which interactions are relevant and when the collective description stops working. The [mathematical programme](/math/) proposes tests and strong failure conditions. This article does not turn those proposed tests into a general theorem. The [stability concept](/concepts/stability/) offers a shorter reading of the same boundary.

## Actual results: a description is not an execution receipt

No new result is derived or reproduced here. Familiar molecules and cells are explanatory examples, while the original documents report particular external and project evidence with their own scope. [Research status](/research-status/) and [the evidence index](/evidence/) distinguish those reports from conjectures and unperformed work.

Treating a cell as a unit in an organism does not imply that all cells or all organisms follow a proved universal equation. Likewise, reported effective interactions do not establish unification of fundamental forces. Whether the organizing principle can be made quantitatively predictive across systems remains open.

A useful next question is concrete: for this interaction and interval, which collective properties suffice, and what observation would force us to describe the parts again? That question preserves the hidden complexity while making the proposed abstraction testable. The separate historical cavity and response calculations remain NOT_SELECTED / NOT_RUN.

---

## Publication orientation — added in the 2026-10-02 audit

**The immediate project is to explain, publish, catalogue evidence and invite contributions—not to require its author to prove universal physics first.** Mathematics and experiments below are optional avenues for contributors. The long-form discussion is retained so the source mechanism, life comparison, expansion idea and engineering implications are not lost through over-compression.

The core remains \(R=(G,M)\), \(G\leftrightarrow M\), and \(B_n\to R_n\to B_{n+1}\). The stronger possibility of one form-invariant equation family is an additional mathematical conjecture, not a new definition of the author’s idea. “Locked” means changes must be explicit and versioned; it does not mean empirically established.

Empirical examples are documented in [06 — Evidence catalogue](06_evidence_catalog.md). [05](05_mathematical_source_model.md) is optional. [08 — Claim and session coverage](08_claim_coverage.md) preserves the full set of ideas and distinguishes them from current evidence. Sections 7, 8, 11, 13–14, 24–25 and 33–43 have explicit audit corrections. Earlier text is preserved in `archive/`.

---

# 0. Why this document exists

The previous RRG documents established the local closure:

\[
\boxed{R=(G,M)}
\]

with:

\[
\boxed{G\leftrightarrow M}
\]

where geometry determines the modes a system can support, and active modes act back on the geometry.

The missing conceptual layer was the **source direction**:

> How can a new resonant geometry appear from a lower-level background, change that background, and thereby create the conditions from which another level can appear?

The central extension developed here is:

\[
\boxed{
B_n
\rightarrow
R_n
\rightarrow
B_{n+1}
\rightarrow
R_{n+1}
\rightarrow\cdots
}
\]

where:

- \(B_n\) is the effective background available at level \(n\),
- \(R_n=(G_n,M_n)\) is a persistent resonant geometry emerging within it,
- the existence of \(R_n\) transforms what later structures experience as their environment,
- the transformed environment can support structures and modes that were not accessible before.

This document is intentionally broader than a mathematical addendum. It records the full conceptual chain, its strongest known physical analogues, the open claims, and the forward research program.

---

# 1. Lock boundary: existing RRG definitions remain unchanged

This document does **not** redefine the core primitives.

## 1.1 Geometry

\[
G=
\{\text{components, positions, connectivity, order, orientation, boundaries, constraints}\}.
\]

Geometry is relational organization, not merely visible Euclidean outline.

## 1.2 Mode

\[
M=
\{\omega,\phi,A,\psi(x),\text{propagation},\text{coupling},\tau,\ldots\}.
\]

In intuitive discussion we often say **frequency**, but the scientific object is the full mode structure: frequency or spectrum, phase, amplitude, spatial pattern, coupling, propagation, and characteristic times.

A mode can be spatial, temporal or both. A stationary pattern is not automatically a temporal resonator. When a paper supplies only a spatial eigenmode or a steady attractor, the catalogue records that narrower result rather than silently treating it as proof of resonant self-maintenance.

## 1.3 Resonant dynamic geometry

\[
\boxed{R=(G,M)}
\]

## 1.4 Dynamic closure / persistence

\[
\boxed{G\rightarrow M\rightarrow G}
\]

A resonant geometry is persistent when its geometry supports a compatible mode structure and those dynamics maintain, restore, or continually recreate the organized state.

## 1.5 Scale

A scale is an effective regime in which a lower-level persistent structure can be treated as an effective unit by the next description level.

This document adds the explicit recursive background object \(B_n\) and makes the source-direction loop central.

---

# 2. Rule 0 — the source-direction statement

The candidate source rule is:

> **In an active background, transient geometries continuously appear. A geometry that supports a mode which reinforces or reconstructs that geometry can persist as a resonant dynamic structure. Persistent resonant structures then become part of the background and boundary conditions from which subsequent structures emerge.**

In compact form:

\[
\boxed{
B_n
\rightarrow
G_n
\leftrightarrow
M_n
\rightarrow
R_n
\rightarrow
B_{n+1}
}
\]

and therefore:

\[
\boxed{
B_0
\rightarrow
R_0
\rightarrow
B_1
\rightarrow
R_1
\rightarrow
B_2
\rightarrow
R_2
\rightarrow\cdots
}
\]

This is the current candidate **Recursive Background Generator**.

The important claim is not that every level looks the same. The claim is that the **same abstract operation** can run in different inherited backgrounds.

---

# 3. Level 0: begin from activity, not from pre-built resonators

The source model should not begin by assuming a universe already full of completed resonators.

Begin instead with the lowest effective background available to the theory:

\[
\boxed{B_0}.
\]

Intuitively, this can be imagined as a fluctuating or noise-like background.

However, **RRG does not yet claim that the physical primordial universe was mathematically ideal white noise**. White noise has a precise meaning: a flat spectrum with very short correlations. The correct scientific term is therefore:

\[
\boxed{\text{effective fluctuating background}}
\]

or, when the approximation is justified:

\[
\boxed{\text{effective noise bath}}.
\]

The conceptual starting point is simply that \(B_0\) contains dynamics before any higher persistent organization has been selected.

Transient configurations continually occur:

\[
B_0
\rightarrow
\{G_0^{(1)},G_0^{(2)},G_0^{(3)},\ldots\}.
\]

Most are temporary.

But if one configuration supports a mode that acts back on the configuration in a stabilizing way:

\[
G_0^{(*)}
\rightarrow
M_0^{(*)}
\rightarrow
G_0^{(*)},
\]

then a closed loop has appeared:

\[
\boxed{R_0=(G_0^{(*)},M_0^{(*)})}.
\]

This is the first essential transition:

\[
\boxed{
\text{fluctuation}
\rightarrow
\text{self-consistent resonant geometry}
\rightarrow
\text{persistence}
}
\]

No separate law saying **"become an object"** is needed if the dynamics themselves contain attractors or stable closed mode–geometry relationships.

---

# 4. The first persistent resonator changes what comes next

Before \(R_0\) existed, the surrounding background was \(B_0\).

After \(R_0\) exists, the environment is not identical anymore.

The resonator:

- scatters and filters existing fluctuations,
- introduces characteristic frequencies and phase relations,
- changes local boundary conditions,
- can store and release energy,
- can alter propagation paths,
- can couple previously weak degrees of freedom,
- can suppress some modes and enhance others,
- can create new spatial or temporal correlations.

Therefore:

\[
\boxed{
(B_0,R_0)
\rightarrow
B_0'
}
\]

and with many persistent level-0 structures:

\[
\boxed{
B_1
=
\mathcal B(B_0,\{R_0\},\text{their interactions/history})
}
\]

The first resonator therefore does not merely survive **inside** the background.

It becomes part of what defines the background experienced by later structures.

This is one of the central additions of v0.2.

---

# 5. Geometry creates mode; mode shapes geometry

The simplest local engine remains:

\[
\boxed{
G\rightarrow M\rightarrow G'
}
\]

or, at closure:

\[
\boxed{
G\leftrightarrow M.
}
\]

A familiar visible example is a vibrating plate covered in sand.

The plate geometry and boundary conditions determine allowed mechanical modes. The mode produces spatially nonuniform motion. Sand grains migrate and accumulate in characteristic regions, producing a visible pattern linked to the mode.

So we already know experimentally that:

\[
\boxed{
\text{mode / vibration}
\rightarrow
\text{reorganization of matter}
\rightarrow
\text{geometry}
}
\]

can occur.

The RRG claim is **not** that sand patterns prove the whole theory.

Their importance is that they make one half of the mechanism directly visible: dynamics can select and impose spatial organization.

The opposite half is equally ordinary: changing the plate's geometry or boundaries changes its allowed vibration spectrum.

Thus the physically familiar pair is:

\[
\boxed{
\text{geometry determines modes}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\text{modes can reorganize geometry/material}
}
\]

RRG asks how far this mutual relationship can be generalized.

---

# 6. Coupled resonators show that one mode can become collective

Another established piece is synchronization.

Coupled pendulums, metronomes, clocks, lasers, electrical oscillators, chemical oscillators, and biological rhythms can phase-lock or form collective modes under suitable coupling.

For mechanical metronomes on a movable platform:

\[
\{R_i\}
\rightarrow
\text{shared platform motion}
\rightarrow
\{R_i\}
\]

and a collective synchronized state can emerge.

The relevant principle is:

\[
\boxed{
\text{individual oscillators}
+
\text{coupling}
\rightarrow
\text{collective resonant mode}
}
\]

This matters for the source model because it shows that larger collective modes do not need to be separately programmed. They can arise from interactions among smaller oscillatory units.

It also corrects an overly simple picture in which one oscillator "commands" all others. Often the shared environment is part of the loop:

\[
R_1,R_2,\ldots,R_N
\rightarrow
B
\rightarrow
R_1,R_2,\ldots,R_N.
\]

The collective mode and the components mutually create one another's dynamical conditions.

---

# 7. Scale matching: why different levels respond to different modes

The session's scale intuition is important but must be stated carefully.

The useful principle is not:

> smaller things are always influenced more strongly.

It is:

> **Different geometries and scales have different natural mode spectra, so they couple selectively to different spatial and temporal patterns.**

In many simple resonators, a characteristic frequency scales schematically like:

\[
\boxed{
f\sim \frac{v}{L}
}
\]

although the exact power law depends on the physical system, dimensions, stiffness, mass distribution, and boundary conditions.

This gives the common tendency:

\[
\boxed{
\text{smaller/faster structures}
\leftrightarrow
\text{higher characteristic frequencies}
}
\]

and:

\[
\boxed{
\text{larger collective structures}
\leftrightarrow
\text{slower collective modes}
}
\]

without claiming this as a universal one-line law for every system.

The earthquake/building example from the conversation illustrates the intended intuition; it is not a measured universal scale law. At smaller scales, the verified microparticle experiment in [06, E03](06_evidence_catalog.md#e03) demonstrates acoustic manipulation. That source supports micrometre particles, not every nano-to-cosmic scale. A size comparison must hold material properties and boundary conditions sufficiently comparable; different classes of resonators can have different scaling. These observations motivate the hierarchy idea without establishing it.

So the deeper point is:

\[
\boxed{
\text{a mode strongly reorganizes degrees of freedom that can couple to that mode}
}
\]

not "sound only affects sand" or "small things require sound".

At molecular, electronic, nuclear, or quantum scales, the relevant mode and coupling channels can be completely different.

---

# 8. Time and persistence matter because influence can accumulate

A transient fluctuation can have only a brief effect.

A persistent resonator can interact with its environment through many cycles. Repetition does not guarantee indefinite energy accumulation: losses, saturation and thresholds can prevent any lasting reorganization. A long lifetime and a long phase-coherence time are also different quantities.

Let:

- \(\tau_R\) = resonator lifetime,
- \(T_R\) = characteristic period,
- \(N_R\sim \tau_R/T_R\) = approximate number of cycles during the lifetime (not necessarily phase-coherent cycles),
- \(C_R\) = effective coupling to surrounding degrees of freedom.

Then a longer-lived, well-coupled resonator has more opportunities to produce cumulative changes.

The qualitative principle is:

\[
\boxed{
\text{persistence}
\times
\text{coupling}
\times
\text{available interaction time}
\rightarrow
\text{historical influence}
}
\]

This does **not** mean that the most stable object always dominates.

A highly stable object may couple almost not at all to its surroundings. A strongly coupled state may destroy itself. A mode may have no compatible substrate on which to act.

The scientifically defensible statement is:

> **Persistence increases the opportunity for environmental influence when a suitable coupling and conversion pathway exist.**

---

# 9. Expansion does not need to be a separate command

A central insight from the session is that **"expand" need not be written as an independent law**.

Suppose a persistent geometry \(G\) supports a mode \(M\):

\[
G\rightarrow M.
\]

Suppose that mode acts on nearby compatible degrees of freedom and makes more geometry compatible with \(G\):

\[
M+\text{background}
\rightarrow
G^+.
\]

If the new geometry supports the same or a compatible mode:

\[
G^+
ightarrow M^+,
\]

then the loop can propagate:

\[
\boxed{
G
\rightarrow
M
\rightarrow
G^+
\rightarrow
M^+
\rightarrow
G^{++}
\rightarrow\cdots
}
\]

This is expansion by **positive feedback**, not because the structure contains an abstract goal to grow.

Required ingredients remain physical:

\[
\boxed{
\text{compatible structure}
+
\text{coupling}
+
\text{available energy/flux when required}
+
\text{accessible substrate}
}
\]

If losses exceed reinforcement, the expansion stops.

If another incompatible stable domain competes for the same degrees of freedom, boundaries or competition can appear.

If several modes are mutually compatible or use different resources, coexistence is possible.

Therefore the framework does **not** assume:

\[
\text{one resonance must conquer everything}.
\]

It predicts a spectrum of possibilities:

\[
\boxed{
\text{decay, persistence, expansion, coexistence, competition, transformation}
}
\]

depending on the actual dynamics.

---

# 10. Selection can emerge without a special selection law

Once multiple persistent structures are possible, differential persistence follows automatically.

Consider candidate resonant structures \(R_i\).

Each has different:

- lifetime,
- coupling,
- resistance to perturbation,
- ability to recruit compatible structure,
- access to energy and substrate,
- compatibility or incompatibility with other structures.

Some disappear quickly.

Some persist.

Some spread.

Some coexist.

Thus an abstract selection process appears:

\[
\boxed{
\text{variation}
\rightarrow
\text{differential persistence}
\rightarrow
\text{different environmental impact}
}
\]

without introducing a separate fundamental command saying **"select the strongest"**.

The word **strongest** should itself be avoided unless the metric is defined. Stability, replication rate, spatial reach, coupling strength, and energetic efficiency are different quantities.

A better statement is:

> **Persistence and propagation can increase a structure’s contribution to its later environment; their importance depends on coupling, resources and the kind of influence being measured. This is not a universal ranking of structures.**

That background is history made physical.

---

# 11. The lower level becomes the effective background of the next

This is the key recursive move, but it contains two different operations.

**Physical change:** realized lower-level structures and their interactions alter the environment. For example, their arrangement can change a field, boundary, chemical condition or transport pathway. This is an actual dynamical effect, whether or not anyone changes their description.

\[
(B_n,\{R_n\}_{\mathrm{realized}},\text{interactions and resources})
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{physical\ evolution}} B_n'.
\]

**Change of description:** at a larger or slower scale, some lower-level detail is unresolved. A reduction then describes selected collective variables and the remaining effective background:

\[
B_{n+1}=\mathcal C_n[B_n',\{R_n\}_{\mathrm{realized}}].
\]

The map \(\mathcal C_n\) does not itself physically make a new structure. A useful higher-level object must also exist and persist in the underlying system. This distinction prevents an ordinary mathematical coarse-graining from being mistaken for evidence of physical recursive construction.

The background may retain characteristic spectra, spatial correlations, memory, boundaries, mean fields and energy exchange. It need not be white noise. Mori’s reduction [06, E14](06_evidence_catalog.md#e14) is a relevant mathematical example of unresolved dynamics appearing as memory and effective fluctuations; it is not a full RRG formation experiment.

This preserves the intended statement:

> **What is organized at one scale can become the material, constraints and unresolved activity from which organization emerges at the next.**

The lower level remains physically active. Several levels can coexist, branch or fail to produce another level.

---

# 12. The same operation can now run again

Once \(B_{n+1}\) exists, new candidate geometries can appear within it:

\[
B_{n+1}
\rightarrow
\{G_{n+1}^{(i)}\}.
\]

Most are transient.

A stable closure produces:

\[
G_{n+1}^{(*)}
\leftrightarrow
M_{n+1}^{(*)}
\]

and therefore:

\[
\boxed{
R_{n+1}
=(G_{n+1}^{(*)},M_{n+1}^{(*)}).
}
\]

Then:

\[
R_{n+1}
\rightarrow
B_{n+2}.
\]

The source operation repeats:

\[
\boxed{
B_n
\rightarrow
R_n
\rightarrow
B_{n+1}.
}
\]

This is the most compact form of the theory developed in this session.

---

# 13. Each level opens a new possibility space

Let:

\[
\boxed{\mathcal P_n}
\]

be the set of dynamically accessible organizations in background \(B_n\).

Because \(R_n\) changes the background:

\[
B_n\rightarrow B_{n+1},
\]

the accessible set can also change:

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal P_n
\rightarrow
\mathcal P_{n+1}.
}
\]

This is more than creating additional copies of old objects.

A new persistent unit can make previously inaccessible combinations feasible under the changed conditions, including:

- combinations,
- relative positions,
- bonds,
- collective phases,
- boundaries,
- frequencies,
- information-bearing states,
- interaction networks,
- catalytic pathways,
- composite geometries.

Therefore:

\[
\boxed{
\text{stable organization}
\rightarrow
\text{new effective degrees of freedom}
\rightarrow
\text{new possible organization}
}
\]

“New effective degrees of freedom” means new useful collective variables or accessible arrangements, not an automatic increase in the underlying microscopic state-space dimension. The accessible set may gain some organizations and lose others; a monotonic size comparison needs a defined measure and matched conditions.

Complexity does not have to be the objective.

It can be a consequence of repeatedly creating reusable stable units.

A more precise slogan is:

\[
\boxed{
\text{complexity becomes a new simple unit for the next scale}.
}
\]

---

# 14. "The previous level already created what it can" — precise version

The intuitive session statement was:

> each level creates what it can; then the stable result creates the space for something new.

The careful version is:

For background \(B_n\), define the stable set:

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal S(B_n)
=
\{R:\ R\text{ is dynamically accessible and persistent under }B_n\}.
}
\]

The level need not literally explore every mathematical possibility.

Instead, the dynamics select some persistent subset of what is accessible.

As that persistent subset becomes part of the environment:

\[
\{R_n\}
\rightarrow
B_{n+1},
\]

the stable set can change:

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal S(B_{n+1})
\neq\mathcal S(B_n).
}
\]

The older reference list is preserved in the archived original. It contained an incomplete attribution of the noise-order review and an overly broad use of a nonresonating-plate study. Reviews are now orientation sources, not additional independent confirmations. Different evidence cards support different pieces; their juxtaposition does not prove the complete causal chain.

---

# 43. Final boundary: what this document claims

This document does **not** claim that the complete Unity/RRG theory has been proved.

It claims that we now have a coherent source-direction hypothesis whose elementary pieces overlap substantially with established physical phenomena:

\[
\boxed{
\text{fluctuation}
\rightarrow
\text{mode/geometry closure}
\rightarrow
\text{persistence}
\rightarrow
\text{background transformation}
\rightarrow
\text{new accessible organization}
}
\]

The distinctive RRG claim is the recursion:

\[
\boxed{
B_n\rightarrow R_n\rightarrow B_{n+1}
}
\]

proposed to repeat across effective levels. A common mathematical family is one stronger way that proposal might eventually be formalized.

The immediate publication offers the explanation, evidence connections, limitations and open questions. Proofs and new experiments are welcome contributions, not conditions for sharing it.

entries.statement: **RRG v0.2.1 · checked 2 October 2026 · living publication companion** RRG proposes that persistent geometry–mode organization can change the background in which further organization becomes possible. This catalogue explains the real observations and limited mathematical results that make parts of that idea worth considering. It does not require a universal proof before the hypothesis is shared. **The key reading rule:** an established component is evidence that a mechanism can occur under the reported conditions. Its interpretation as one stage of RRG is a separate claim. Different examples do not automatically combine into one demonstrated recursive chain. ## Two labels, not one evidence ladder **What kind of result?** Experiment; simulation; theoretical/mathematical derivation. A study can contain more than one. A review is an orientation source rather than an extra experiment. Internal RRG calculations are separately labelled and not counted as independent support. **How does it relate?** A *component* demonstrates a local operation; a *partial bridge* connects operations in one system; an *analogy* shares organizational logic without demonstrating the same microscopic process; a *constraint/comparator* identifies limits or an alternative mechanism. None of these labels is a confidence score for all of RRG. ## Claim map | Claim | Limited operation being discussed | |---|---| | C0 | Fluctuations or a uniform starting regime can participate in pattern formation or interaction. | | C1 | Geometry and mode structure constrain or affect one another. | | C2 | Coupled oscillators can develop collective phase/frequency relationships. | | C3 | A driven field or vibration can reorganize material. | | C4 | An organization, boundary or interaction changes what its surroundings can do. | | C5 | A nonliving pattern or chemical organization can propagate or multiply. | | C6 | Lower-level dynamics admit useful collective variables and an effective background description. | | C7 | Controlled conditions can implement selected effective dynamics. | These are not eight already-proved stages in the history of the universe. C0, for example, distinguishes noise-induced ordering from deterministic instability. C6 distinguishes a physical new environment from our mathematical description of it. ## Start with these connections For the source-direction intuition, begin with **E19** (random-field-mediated interaction) and **E04** (noise-assisted pattern formation in a model). For reciprocal organization, use **E07/E08/E18**. For multiplication without life, use **E10/E11/E20**. For the next-level background, read **E14/E21** together with their limits. E17 and E22 prevent the catalogue from turning all organization into evidence for stronger resonance. ## Case index | ID | Example | Result type | Relation | |---|---|---|---| | [E01](#e01) | Mechanical synchronization (2015) | experiment | component / constraint | | [E02](#e02) | Chladni particle manipulation (2016) | experiment | component | | [E03](#e03) | Acoustic microparticle trapping (2014) | experiment | component | | [E04](#e04) | Noise-assisted patterning model (2005) | simulation | component | | [E05](#e05) | Stationary Turing patterns (1991) | experiment | component / comparator | | [E06](#e06) | Forced chemical patterns (1997) | experiment | partial bridge | | [E07](#e07) | Atom–cavity self-organization (2010) | experiment | partial bridge | | [E08](#e08) | Colloidal swarmalators (2025) | experiment | partial bridge | | [E09](#e09) | Simulated resonance selection (2017) | simulation | partial bridge | | [E10](#e10) | Replicating chemical spots (1994) | experiment | partial bridge | | [E11](#e11) | Replicating suspension holes (2011) | experiment | partial bridge | | [E12](#e12) | Driven magnetic assembly (2000) | experiment | partial bridge | | [E13](#e13) | Cooperative RNA networks (2012) | experiment | structural analogue / partial bridge | | [E14](#e14) | Collective reduction and memory (1965) | theory / mathematical derivation | partial bridge | | [E15](#e15) | Engineered lattice dynamics (2013) | experiment | partial bridge | | [E16](#e16) | Confinement-dependent packing (2023) | experiment and simulation | component / comparator | | [E17](#e17) | Low-absorption selection (2023) | simulation; published report also includes experimental evidence | constraint | | [E18](#e18) | Optical binding (1989) | experiment | partial bridge | | [E19](#e19) | Random-light interactions (2015) | experiment and theory | partial bridge | | [E20](#e20) | Replicating granular bands (2024) | experiment | partial bridge | | [E21](#e21) | Controlled amplitude approximation (2026) | theory / mathematical derivation | partial bridge | | [E22](#e22) | Nonresonant granular transport (2026) | experiment | constraint / comparator | ## E01 — Experimental Study of the Triplet Synchronization of Coupled Nonidentical Mechanical Metronomes **experiment · component / constraint · claims C2.** **Reported result:** Coupled nonidentical metronomes exhibit a collective triplet synchronization relation even where individual pairs are asynchronous. **Already supplied:** Metronomes, their energy supply, and mechanical coupling already exist. **Limit of the RRG connection:** Collective coordination need not mean every oscillator has one identical frequency or phase. This does not demonstrate the creation of the oscillators. **Source:** Jia, Song, Liu, Kurths & Xiao (2015), *Scientific Reports 5, 17008*. [DOI: 10.1038/srep17008](https://doi.org/10.1038/srep17008). **Verification coverage:** Publisher HTML, including experimental description. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E02 — Controlling the motion of multiple objects on a Chladni plate **experiment · component · claims C1, C3.** **Reported result:** Plate vibrations can transport particles; the study uses controlled sequences of excitation to manipulate multiple objects. **Already supplied:** A manufactured plate, particles, actuator, camera and control algorithm are provided. **Limit of the RRG connection:** Distinguish ordinary nodal accumulation from the paper’s actively controlled manipulation. Neither establishes autonomous particle-to-field feedback or reproduction. **Source:** Zhou, Sariola, Latifi & Liimatainen (2016), *Nature Communications 7, 12764*. [DOI: 10.1038/ncomms12764](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms12764). **Verification coverage:** Publisher HTML and author-institution abstract. Supplementary videos linked on the paper page were not watched. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E03 — Independent trapping and manipulation of microparticles using dexterous acoustic tweezers **experiment · component · claims C3.** **Reported result:** A phased ultrasonic array independently traps and manipulates microparticles; reported examples include 45 and 90 micrometre spheres. **Already supplied:** An engineered transducer array, liquid medium and pre-existing particles are required. **Limit of the RRG connection:** This particular experiment supports microscale manipulation, not a claim of nanoscale performance or a universal size–frequency law. **Source:** Courtney et al. (2014), *Applied Physics Letters 104, 154103*. [DOI: 10.1063/1.4870489](https://doi.org/10.1063/1.4870489). **Verification coverage:** Author-institution records and original-paper abstract; not a full methods or data audit. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E04 — Noise-induced spatial periodicity in excitable chemical media **simulation · component · claims C0.** **Reported result:** Numerical excitable-chemical-media dynamics show an intermediate noise regime with enhanced spatial periodicity. **Already supplied:** An Oregonator-type reaction model, diffusion, parameter choices and noisy forcing are specified. **Limit of the RRG connection:** This is a numerical result, not a laboratory observation of the primordial background. Noise acts through existing nonlinear dynamics. **Source:** Matjaž Perc (2005), *Chemical Physics Letters 410, 49–53*. [DOI: 10.1016/j.cplett.2005.05.042](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cplett.2005.05.042). **Verification coverage:** Primary publisher record and abstract; equations and simulation data not independently reproduced. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E05 — Transition from a uniform state to hexagonal and striped Turing patterns **experiment · component / comparator · claims C0.** **Reported result:** A chemically supplied reaction–diffusion experiment produces stationary patterned states from a uniform regime. **Already supplied:** Specific reactions, diffusion, gel geometry and reagent supply are provided. **Limit of the RRG connection:** A stationary spatial mode is not automatically a temporal oscillation or a self-maintaining resonator. Uniform-state instability is not identical to noise-induced ordering. **Source:** Ouyang & Swinney (1991), *Nature 352, 610–612*. [DOI: 10.1038/352610a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/352610a0). **Verification coverage:** Publisher abstract and bibliographic record. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E06 — Resonant pattern formation in a chemical system **experiment · partial bridge · claims C2, C3.** **Reported result:** Periodic illumination of a photosensitive chemical oscillator locks responses to the forcing and changes the spatial pattern. **Already supplied:** The reaction medium and periodic optical drive are supplied externally. **Limit of the RRG connection:** The experiment links temporal forcing and spatial organization, not the spontaneous origin of the drive or new fundamental laws. **Source:** Petrov, Ouyang & Swinney (1997), *Nature 388, 655–657*. [DOI: 10.1038/41732](https://doi.org/10.1038/41732). **Verification coverage:** Publisher abstract and record. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E07 — Dicke quantum phase transition with a superfluid gas in an optical cavity **experiment · partial bridge · claims C1, C3, C4.** **Reported result:** A pumped atom–cavity system undergoes a collective transition with mutually coupled matter organization and optical-field dynamics. **Already supplied:** Atoms, cavity boundaries and laser pumping are given. **Limit of the RRG connection:** This is a close geometry–field feedback example, but not unstructured matter producing its own complete apparatus or successive autonomous levels. **Source:** Baumann, Guerlin, Brennecke & Esslinger (2010), *Nature 464, 1301–1306*. [DOI: 10.1038/nature09009](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09009). **Verification coverage:** Publisher abstract and article record. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E08 — Tunable colloidal swarmalators with hydrodynamic coupling **experiment · partial bridge · claims C1, C2, C3.** **Reported result:** Colloidal oscillator phases and spatial organization co-evolve in collective states. **Already supplied:** Feedback-controlled active particles and hydrodynamic interactions are part of the experimental mechanism. **Limit of the RRG connection:** The control architecture is essential context; it cannot be omitted when describing how spontaneous the organization is. **Source:** Heuthe, Iyer, Gompper & Bechinger (2025), *Nature Communications 16, 10984*. [DOI: 10.1038/s41467-025-66830-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-66830-5). **Verification coverage:** Publisher HTML, including setup/control description. Checked 2026-10-02. Published 8 December 2025. The experiment is not a demonstration of an unprogrammed universal source law. ## E09 — Self-Organized Resonance during Search of a Diverse Chemical Space **simulation · partial bridge · claims C1, C4.** **Reported result:** A driven reacting-particle model develops structures matched to periodic forcing; in the studied regime their energy absorption helps stabilization. **Already supplied:** Toy reaction rules, Brownian dynamics and a periodic drive are specified. **Limit of the RRG connection:** This is not laboratory evidence and does not show that maximum absorption is a universal selection rule. Compare E17. **Source:** Kachman, Owen & England (2017), *Physical Review Letters 119, 038001*. [DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.038001](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.038001). **Verification coverage:** Original-paper abstract on APS and author-institution record. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E10 — Experimental observation of self-replicating spots in a reaction–diffusion system **experiment · partial bridge · claims C5.** **Reported result:** Chemical spots grow and split repeatedly in a laboratory reaction–diffusion system. **Already supplied:** Reactive chemicals and nonequilibrium experimental conditions are supplied. **Limit of the RRG connection:** Pattern duplication is not automatically reproduction with heredity, or a new organizational level. Do not infer a resonant microscopic mechanism merely from the shared shape of the process. **Source:** Lee, McCormick, Pearson & Swinney (1994), *Nature 369, 215–218*. [DOI: 10.1038/369215a0](https://doi.org/10.1038/369215a0). **Verification coverage:** Publisher abstract and bibliographic record. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E11 — Self-Replicating Holes in a Vertically Vibrated Dense Suspension **experiment · partial bridge · claims C3, C5.** **Reported result:** Holes in a vertically driven starch suspension deform and split under suitable forcing. **Already supplied:** The suspension, container and sustained vertical vibration already exist. **Limit of the RRG connection:** A hole is a spatial pattern in supplied material, not a newly manufactured independent resonator or organism. Shape instability is part of replication here. **Source:** Ebata & Sano (2011), *Physical Review Letters 107, 088301*. [DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.088301](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.088301). **Verification coverage:** Original-paper abstract on APS. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E12 — Dynamic self-assembly of magnetized, millimetre-sized objects rotating at a liquid–air interface **experiment · partial bridge · claims C3, C4.** **Reported result:** Magnetically driven objects organize through their motion and fluid-mediated interactions. **Already supplied:** Fabricated magnetic objects, liquid interface and rotating external field are provided. **Limit of the RRG connection:** The result connects maintained activity and spatial arrangement. It does not imply all stable structures need continuous external driving. **Source:** Grzybowski, Stone & Whitesides (2000), *Nature 405, 1033–1036*. [DOI: 10.1038/35016528](https://doi.org/10.1038/35016528). **Verification coverage:** Publisher abstract and bibliographic record. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E13 — Spontaneous network formation among cooperative RNA replicators **experiment · structural analogue / partial bridge · claims C5, C4.** **Reported result:** RNA fragments assemble into catalytic networks; tested cooperative networks have growth advantages over competing autocatalytic cycles. **Already supplied:** Selected RNA sequences, fragments and controlled chemical conditions are supplied. **Limit of the RRG connection:** This supports chemical organizational feedback and cooperation, not an identical acoustic or fundamental-particle mechanism. A formal catalytic graph alone does not establish sustained kinetics. **Source:** Vaidya, Manapat, Chen, Xulvi-Brunet, Hayden & Lehman (2012), *Nature 491, 72–77*. [DOI: 10.1038/nature11549](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature11549). **Verification coverage:** Publisher abstract and change history; full subscription methods not inspected. Checked 2026-10-02. Publisher reports a minor Figure 1 typo corrected on 31 October 2012. No claim here depends on the corrected figure. ## E14 — Transport, Collective Motion, and Brownian Motion **theory / mathematical derivation · partial bridge · claims C6.** **Reported result:** Projection of many-body dynamics leads to a reduced description involving collective variables, memory and effective fluctuating forces. **Already supplied:** Microscopic dynamics and a projection/choice of resolved variables are supplied. **Limit of the RRG connection:** Unresolved dynamics need not be white noise. Describing a system at lower resolution does not physically create a new medium or hierarchy. **Source:** Hazime Mori (1965), *Progress of Theoretical Physics 33, 423–455*. [DOI: 10.1143/PTP.33.423](https://doi.org/10.1143/PTP.33.423). **Verification coverage:** Original publisher abstract and record; historical derivation not independently re-proved. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E15 — Realization of the Hofstadter Hamiltonian with Ultracold Atoms in Optical Lattices **experiment · partial bridge · claims C7.** **Reported result:** Laser-assisted tunnelling implements an effective lattice Hamiltonian with magnetic-field-like phases. **Already supplied:** Cold atoms, an optical lattice and precisely controlled driving are provided. **Limit of the RRG connection:** This demonstrates selected effective dynamics, not arbitrary alteration of fundamental laws or a frequency-only recipe. **Source:** Aidelsburger, Atala, Lohse, Barreiro, Paredes & Bloch (2013), *Physical Review Letters 111, 185301*. [DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.185301](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.111.185301). **Verification coverage:** Original-paper abstract on APS. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E16 — A colloidal viewpoint on the sausage catastrophe and the finite sphere packing problem **experiment and simulation · component / comparator · claims C4.** **Reported result:** Confinement of colloidal spheres in vesicles influences which packing geometries occur, including competing arrangements. **Already supplied:** Pre-existing particles, confining membranes and their material properties are provided. **Limit of the RRG connection:** This is evidence that geometry affects accessible organization, not evidence that every such effect requires resonance. **Source:** Marín-Aguilar et al. (2023), *Nature Communications 14, 7896*. [DOI: 10.1038/s41467-023-43722-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-43722-0). **Verification coverage:** Publisher HTML; not an independent reproduction of simulations. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E17 — Drive-specific selection in multistable mechanical networks **simulation; published report also includes experimental evidence · constraint · claims C4.** **Reported result:** In studied driven mechanical networks, selected configurations absorb relatively little work from the drive. **Already supplied:** Multistable spring networks, their interaction landscape and an external drive are supplied. **Limit of the RRG connection:** This constrains “strongest resonance always dominates”; it does not refute a conditional geometry–mode hypothesis. The experimental portion was not separately method-audited here. **Source:** Kedia, Pan, Slotine & England (2023), *Journal of Chemical Physics 159, 214106*. [DOI: 10.1063/5.0171993](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0171993). **Verification coverage:** Author preprint arXiv:1908.09332 plus journal metadata and original abstract indexed by PubMed. Checked 2026-10-02. The 2019 preprint title is Drive-specific adaptation in disordered mechanical networks of bistable springs. It is not an additional independent study. ## E18 — Optical binding **experiment · partial bridge · claims C3, C4.** **Reported result:** Illuminated microspheres display light-mediated interactions and bound configurations. **Already supplied:** An external optical field, microspheres and surrounding medium already exist. **Limit of the RRG connection:** Field scattering and particle arrangement interact, but a bound pair is not yet a recursively reproducing hierarchy. **Source:** Burns, Fournier & Golovchenko (1989), *Physical Review Letters 63, 1233–1236*. [DOI: 10.1103/PhysRevLett.63.1233](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.63.1233). **Verification coverage:** Original-paper abstract and record on APS. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E19 — Controlling dispersion forces between small particles with artificially created random light fields **experiment and theory · partial bridge · claims C0, C4.** **Reported result:** Artificially generated random light produces measured attractive interactions between dielectric microspheres. **Already supplied:** Pre-existing spheres and a laser-generated, quasi-monochromatic random optical field are provided. **Limit of the RRG connection:** Random does not mean broadband white noise. The experiment supports fluctuation-mediated interaction, not spontaneous creation of the spheres; broader interaction designs include theoretical proposals. **Source:** Brügger, Froufe-Pérez, Scheffold & Sáenz (2015), *Nature Communications 6, 7460*. [DOI: 10.1038/ncomms8460](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms8460). **Verification coverage:** Publisher HTML, including experimental versus theoretical scope. Checked 2026-10-02. ## E20 — Self-replicating segregation patterns in horizontally vibrated binary mixture of granules **experiment · partial bridge · claims C3, C4, C5.** **Reported result:** A shaken granular mixture develops bands that reproduce; segregation and flow/fluidity feedback participate in the dynamics. **Already supplied:** Two grain populations, a container and continued horizontal shaking are supplied. **Limit of the RRG connection:** This connects vibration, organization and pattern multiplication without biological copying machinery. It does not establish successive independent scales. **Source:** Ebata & Inagaki (2024), *Scientific Reports 14, 5329*. [DOI: 10.1038/s41598-024-55876-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-55876-y). **Verification coverage:** Publisher HTML. Supplementary materials were not independently reproduced. Checked 2026-10-02. Shares an author with E11; these are different systems, not independent replications of a single result. ## E21 — Pattern formation in a Swift-Hohenberg equation with spatially periodic coefficients **theory / mathematical derivation · partial bridge · claims C6.** **Reported result:** A slow-amplitude description is justified for a specified pattern-forming equation near onset, under stated spectral and coefficient assumptions. **Already supplied:** The equation, spatially periodic coefficients and near-instability regime are specified. **Limit of the RRG connection:** A controlled change of scale in description is not an unlimited sequence of new physical levels. The environmental heterogeneity is given, not derived from the emerging pattern. **Source:** Kamphuis & Chirilus-Bruckner (2026), *Physica D 493, 135239*. [DOI: 10.1016/j.physd.2026.135239](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.physd.2026.135239). **Verification coverage:** Publisher HTML, including assumptions and approximation result. Not an independent formal proof check. Checked 2026-10-02. 2026 paper available by this audit; September 2026 issue. ## E22 — Thermodynamics of bouncing grains **experiment · constraint / comparator · claims C3, C6.** **Reported result:** Grain transport is measured on a heterogeneous, nonresonating vibrating plate; effective statistical and transport descriptions are studied. **Already supplied:** A driven plate, heterogeneity and grains are provided. **Limit of the RRG connection:** Vibration-induced transport is not by itself proof of resonance. The earlier document incorrectly grouped this study as an unqualified resonant-mode example. **Source:** Devauchelle, Popović, Szymczak, Abramian & Lazarus (2026), *Physical Review E 114, 025420*. [DOI: 10.1103/zlsc-w7m4](https://doi.org/10.1103/zlsc-w7m4). **Verification coverage:** Original-paper abstract on APS; no raw-data reanalysis. Checked 2026-10-02. APS publication date: 24 August 2026; later index/crawl dates are not used as publication dates. ## What the catalogue does not yet supply There is no documented complete example in this release of unstructured activity producing a resonator, that resonator causally creating another distinct persistent level, and the process continuing indefinitely under one unchanged microscopic rule. This is a limit of the collected evidence, not a claim that no such system can exist or a reason to stop publishing the hypothesis. The highest-value additions would connect adjacent operations in the **same system**. Useful observations would compare an environment before and after an emergent structure forms, identify how its response changes, and show what new organization becomes stable. Negative cases—termination, destruction, coexistence and shrinking scales—are informative too. No source count is a probability of truth. Papers sharing a model, apparatus, authors or data are not automatically independent confirmations. Ordinary explanations of these experiments remain valid competitors; calling them RRG-compatible does not make them RRG-specific evidence. ## Optional mathematics and internal simulations [05 — Optional mathematical illustrations](05_mathematical_source_model.md) contains conditional calculations, not a proof of the full mechanism or an empirical evidence entry. Earlier internal simulations are preserved under `archive/`; their numerical claims were not rerun or independently recertified in this audit. ## Further reading, kept separate from primary case cards **F01 — Spatiotemporal order out of noise**, Francesc Sagués, José M. Sancho & Jordi García-Ojalvo (2007). Review / orientation only. [DOI: 10.1103/RevModPhys.79.829](https://doi.org/10.1103/RevModPhys.79.829). Corrects incomplete or incorrect authorship in prior notes. Review content is not counted as an additional independent experiment. **F02 — Engineering precise and robust effective Hamiltonians**, Chen & Cory (2026). Theory / further reading. [DOI: 10.1103/j65l-f8lf](https://doi.org/10.1103/j65l-f8lf). The previously cited article exists. Retained as optional reading, not dismissed as fabricated or treated as experimental evidence. Published 2 April 2026. **F03 — Validity of the stochastic Ginzburg-Landau approximation in higher space dimensions: A Wiener algebra approach**, Logioti & Schneider (2026). Theory / date-qualified further reading. [DOI: 10.1016/j.jde.2026.114601](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jde.2026.114601). Online publisher record and abstract available at audit. Issue date is 25 October 2026, later than this audit; first-online date was not independently established. Result assumes specific anisotropic periodic domains and regularity of the noise, not arbitrary space-time white noise. ## Videos, data and reuse A video can make a reported effect understandable but is not a substitute for identifying the apparatus, conditions and original paper. Supplementary material was not watched or reproduced in this audit. Link to original paper pages rather than presenting third-party compilations as evidence. Do not copy figures or movies into the public website without checking their licences; a citation is not a reuse licence. ## Adding or changing a case Record the claim ID, original source, result type, actual finding, supplied conditions, RRG interpretation, important alternative explanation, limit, publication date and what was inspected. Mark preprints as preprints; do not count a preprint and its journal version twice. Check the publisher’s correction/retraction notices when visible, and record any unresolved check. This release is not a complete retraction-database or raw-data audit. Keep a prior entry when revising it and state the reason in the changelog. Updates happen when the project is reviewed; no automatic monitoring is running. A failed search is an evidence gap, not proof of absence. **Publication position:** present the proposed common connection confidently as a hypothesis, give established examples their proper scope, and invite explanations, objections, additional cases and optional derivations.

**RRG v0.2.1 · 2 October 2026**

This map prevents two kinds of drift: losing the author’s bigger idea when tightening scientific language, and turning a proposed connection into a verified fact. “Preserved” means the idea remains in the publication, not that it has been established.

## Session coverage

| ID | Idea from the discussion | Where retained | Current status / important boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| H01 | Start with fluctuating activity, not pre-built resonators | 04 §§2–4 | Source hypothesis. A fluctuating background still needs defined dynamics in an implementation. |
| H02 | Transient arrangements appear; some become persistent | 04 §§2–5, 18 | Component precedents E04/E05. These do not establish the primordial origin of matter. |
| H03 | Geometry and frequency/mode form a feedback loop | 04 §§1, 5, 19 | Core proposal; E07/E08 are partial physical bridges. Preserve the full mode definition. |
| H04 | Oscillators influence one another through a shared medium | 04 §6; E01 | Experimental component. Collective synchronization need not mean identical phases/frequencies. |
| H05 | Vibration can rearrange suitable material | 04 §7; E02/E03/E20 | Experimental component under stated coupling and forcing. Not every rearrangement is resonant. |
| H06 | A formed structure reshapes the background around it | 04 §§4, 11, 24 | Key causal connection; partial bridges E07/E18/E19, with supplied apparatus explicit. |
| H07 | Longer persistence gives more opportunity to influence | 04 §8 | Conditional interpretation, not inevitable growth or indefinitely accumulated energy. |
| H08 | Repeated compatible arrangements can appear without a copying command | 04 §§9–10 | Proposed mechanism. Recurrence, synchronization, recruitment and independent reproduction differ. |
| H09 | Domains compete, dominate or coexist | 04 §§9–10 | Conditional outcomes, not a single “strongest frequency always wins” law. E17 constrains it. |
| H10 | Lower-level organization becomes noise-like substrate to the next level | 04 §11; E14 | Core conjectural use of effective background. Noise can be correlated and retain memory. |
| H11 | The same abstract operation repeats in different effective worlds | 04 §§12, 21, 25, 41 | Central RRG hypothesis, not established by combining unrelated examples. |
| H12 | Persistent combinations become new effective units | 04 §§12–13, 22 | Proposed hierarchy. A larger synchronized patch alone is not proof of a new unit. |
| H13 | Stable units enable new organizational possibilities | 04 §§13–14 | Accessible possibilities can change. No universal monotonic measure has been established. |
| H14 | A level creates available stable organizations before later combinations become feasible | 04 §14 | Preserve the intuition; not literal exhaustion of all states or a universal sequential timetable. |
| H15 | New geometry/background defines new effective rules | 04 §§15–16, 29; E15 | Effective behavior is distinguishable from replacement of fundamental equations. |
| H16 | One source may ultimately account for the fundamental interactions | 04 §§35–39; O4 below | Retained as ambitious conjecture; no four-force derivation is claimed. |
| H17 | Life is a visible later instance of organization reconstructing itself | 04 §§17, 30; E13 | Structural analogy and chemical partial bridges; no identical microscopic-mechanism claim. |
| H18 | New scales may relate to the expansion and evolution of the universe | 04 §§26–28; O5 below | Preserve the proposed connection; physical metric expansion needs separate support. |
| H19 | Work forward from the source rather than merely reinterpreting finished structures | 04 §§2–4, 40–41 | Methodological preference. Existing observations and reverse constraints can still test the proposal. |
| H20 | Control modes to control organization and effective behavior—“magic” | 04 §§31–32; O6 below | Retained speculative engineering vision. E15 supports selected effective dynamics, not unlimited control. |
| H21 | Information might specify a useful mode/geometry/state | 04 §32 | Open engineering idea. A frequency alone is not a universal shape code. |
| H22 | The idea may inform AI, learning and abstraction | AI note below; foundation 01 §AI and 02 §10 | Retained application hypothesis. Useful intelligence or learning does not follow from persistence alone. |
| H23 | Publish, collect cases, review and update; proofs welcome but optional | README; 04 §40; 06 update practice | Current project workflow. No autonomous monitoring or proof-before-publication gate. |

## Open-claim registry

**O1 — Recursive physical construction.** One formed organization causes conditions for another distinct persistent organization, and this repeats. A useful contribution could document even two causally connected stages in one system. No such full universal chain is established by this catalogue.

**O2 — Same principle across levels.** The author proposes the repeated geometry–mode/background relation. Approximate invariance of an equation family is a stronger optional formalization; identical microscopic mechanisms across chemistry, matter and life are stronger still. These should not be silently conflated.

**O3 — Scale, lifetime and possibility-space growth.** Later levels may often be larger, slower or capable of different organization. Whether any measure grows monotonically is unproved. Levels can coexist; an implementation may stop, branch, shrink or lose stability. New effective coordinates do not automatically add fundamental microscopic dimensions.

**O4 — Fundamental unification.** A deeper common generator might account for the known interactions. Existing synchronization, optical binding or effective-Hamiltonian results do not derive that claim. It remains part of the author’s ambition rather than being removed for lack of proof.

**O5 — Cosmological connection.** The author’s conjecture is that continued formation of scales and organization could connect to the universe’s spatial expansion. Domain growth, increasing organizational depth, increasing accessible configurations and spacetime metric expansion are four different claims. The last is not proved by the first three. This release does not advance a new cosmological calculation or fresh observational cosmology review.

**O6 — Engineered domains.** Speculative “magic” means advanced control of effective physical behavior through organization and mode structure, not a claim of demonstrated supernatural effects. Controllable effective dynamics are real in selected settings (E15); a self-propagating domain with an arbitrarily selected rule set is an open extrapolation.

**O7 — Life and evolution.** Chemical cooperative organization and nonliving pattern duplication supply informative analogies. Biological heredity, evolutionary dynamics and planetary environmental change are not reduced to one measured resonant mechanism here. The universal relation is a hypothesis about organizational form, not an assertion that all systems are living or intentional.

**O8 — AI.** Persistent dynamic modules and activity-dependent relations suggest a possible architecture. In this release no RRG AI model is benchmarked and no gain in intelligence, transfer or efficiency is established. A later contribution should distinguish stable activity from useful prediction or learning. This proposal remains available without becoming a proof requirement for the physics framework.

## How evidence changes a claim

A component observation supports the possibility of that component under its conditions. A measured causal sequence strengthens a bridge. A discriminating prediction could strengthen a specified RRG implementation relative to alternatives. A failure of a particular model addresses that model; a counterexample to a precise universal claim addresses that claim. Neither success nor failure should automatically be generalized to every statement above.

Lack of a universal proof is not a reason to remove the proposed connection from a clearly labelled hypothesis publication. It is a reason to distinguish the connection from its supporting examples.

## In ordinary words

An effective interaction is part of a description of a collective system. Existing organization, fields and boundaries can change which interactions are available. RRG asks whether such changes can help further organization persist.

## Two distinct source-reported cases

- **Optical binding:** illuminated microspheres show light-mediated interactions and bound arrangements. The light, particles and medium are already supplied. :claim[UT-E118]
- **Controlled random light:** an artificially generated random optical field produces measured attractive interactions between small spheres. Random does not mean broadband white noise, and the experiment does not create the spheres. :claim[UT-E119]

These are component connections in specified systems, not a complete autonomous sequence of new levels. The [catalogue](/evidence/catalogue/) preserves the reported observations, supplied conditions, result types and inspection limits.

## The proposed relation

The conditional proposal can be written schematically:

$$
R_n=(G_n,M_n)\;\rightarrow\;\mathcal I^{\rm eff}_{n+1}\;\rightarrow\;R_{n+1}.
$$

Organization can change a background; that background can change which interactions and arrangements persist. The [recursive background companion](/framework/recursive-background/) preserves this proposed connection. Physical environmental change differs from our coarse-graining a description.

## What remains open

The selected [claim coverage](/research-status/claims/) retains fundamental unification, recursive construction, cosmology, life and AI as open claims or analogies. Controlled effective behavior does not establish arbitrary replacement of fundamental laws. No experiment or paper audit was performed by this website.

## In ordinary words

An organized whole can participate in another organization. Its internal activity continues even when the next description treats it as one useful unit. RRG calls this structural recursion.

## A concrete example

The [molecule example](/examples/molecule/) begins with atoms and their connections. A molecule can enter a larger chemical arrangement. A [cell](/examples/cell/) can participate in a tissue while exchanges and reactions continue inside it. These systems have different mechanisms; the shared description does not require identical equations at every scale.

**Scale** means a level at which a collective organization can function as an effective unit in further interactions. It involves characteristic times, dominant interactions and useful descriptions, as well as size. It is not a claim that all levels are equally spaced or every larger process is slower.

The proposed cycle is compatible parts → collective organization → a useful unit → further combinations. Its environment can also change which combinations are accessible. The cycle illustration represents a research proposal, not a measurement or guaranteed history.

::claim{id="UT-D09" view="plainLanguage"}

## In ordinary words

An organization can persist while activity continues inside it. In the supplied core, stability means that geometry and mode structure form a self-consistent closed organization during the interval in question. Persistence may be short or long.

## Compare the questions

A molecule can be considered over a particular lifetime; a living cell needs ongoing exchanges. To test a specified model, we may measure how long a state lasts, how it responds to a perturbation or whether nearby states approach it.

**Bounded persistence** asks whether the chosen organization remains within stated limits over an interval. **Recovery** asks whether it returns after a disturbance. **Attraction** asks whether nearby states tend toward it. These describe different tests; observing one is not automatically a result about the others.

The framework allows different mathematical tests for different systems. They do not replace its locked meaning. A self-consistency definition is not an independently established universal stability theorem.

## The source definition

::claim{id="UT-D04" view="statement"}

Here $G$ denotes organization and $M$ the full temporal mode structure. Their reciprocal relation is the RRG definition being used. A particular application still needs its conditions, equations and evidence; the definition alone does not give a numerical threshold.

entries.statement:
This document prevents theory drift.

## A. Research does not redefine the core

Every new paper, example, analogy, equation, or simulation must be classified as one of:

1. **Supports core** — example fits an existing locked statement.
2. **Tests core** — provides a measurable way to challenge a locked statement.
3. **Extension** — adds a hypothesis downstream of the core without modifying it.
4. **Implementation** — one mathematical/mechanical realization of the core.
5. **Counterexample candidate** — appears to conflict and must pass the proof gate below.
6. **Rejected drift** — introduces a narrower or different definition without necessity.

## B. Proof gate before changing a definition

A core definition can change only if this template is completed:

- **Locked statement:** exact quote.
- **Counterexample:** exact physical/mathematical system.
- **Why it fails:** demonstrate why the system cannot fit the current definition.
- **Evidence:** primary literature, experiment, or derivation.
- **Extension test:** show why adding a downstream condition cannot handle it.
- **Minimal revision:** smallest possible edit.
- **Regression analysis:** list every previous example/claim affected.
- **Decision:** accept/reject, with version bump if accepted.

No completed proof gate = no core change.

## C. Examples never become definitions automatically

Examples such as atoms, molecules, stars, cells, DNA, organisms, brains, gravity, or AI illustrate the core. None of them may be used to narrow the core unless a proof-gate contradiction is established.

For example:

- A multicellular organism made from differentiated cells is **not** an edge case because RRG never requires identical components.
- A radioactive nucleus is **not** an edge case because RRG stability never meant permanence.
- A stationary field configuration is **not** automatically an edge case because RRG mode structure is broader than a visible periodic motion.

## D. Mathematics is subordinate to the locked meaning

A mathematical model is a candidate realization, not a new definition.

- Lyapunov/Floquet criteria may test a particular form of stability but do not redefine RRG stability.
- A lifetime threshold may be useful operationally but cannot define existence or stability.
- A coarse-graining threshold may identify useful effective units but cannot redefine "scale".
- Requiring the same microscopic equation at every scale is an optional strong hypothesis, not the RRG core.
- An effective action \(\Gamma\), spectral operator, Koopman spectrum, RG flow, etc. may model parts of RRG but cannot become the ontology by default.

## E. Research objective

Research should answer:

> Does the locked geometry↔mode framework generate correct predictions, useful reductions, or new unifying relations across multiple domains?

It should **not** continuously rewrite the question until every example fits.

entries.statement:
**Status:** normative core.  
**Rule:** downstream examples, research papers, mathematical models, and analogies may **test or extend** this file but may not silently redefine it.

## 1. Geometry \(G\)

In RRG, **geometry** means the organization of a system at a chosen scale:

\[
G=\{\text{components, arrangement, relations, connectivity, order, orientation, boundaries, constraints}\}.
\]

Geometry is not limited to visible Euclidean shape.

## 2. Frequency / mode structure \(M\)

In RRG, **frequency** is shorthand for the system's full temporal mode organization, not one scalar value in hertz:

\[
M=\{\omega,\phi,A,\psi,\text{propagation, coupling, characteristic timescales, response}\}.
\]

A scalar frequency alone is never assumed to uniquely determine a geometry.

## 3. Resonant geometry \(R\)

The basic RRG object is:

\[
\boxed{R=(G,M)}.
\]

Geometry and mode structure are inseparable aspects of one organized system:

\[
\boxed{G\leftrightarrow M}.
\]

- Geometry constrains/supports which modes can exist.
- The active mode structure supports, maintains, transforms, or destroys the geometry.

Neither side is defined as universally "first".

## 4. Stability

**Locked definition:** a geometry is stable in RRG while its geometry and mode structure form a self-consistent closed organization:

\[
\boxed{G\leftrightarrow M}.
\]

Stability is **not permanence**. A state may satisfy the closure for a very short or very long interval.

Lifetime, perturbation recovery, Lyapunov stability, decay width, or metastability are **measurements/tests of a particular system**, not replacements for this core definition.

## 5. Higher-level formation

A higher-level resonant geometry may be formed from any compatible collection of lower-level resonant geometries:

\[
\boxed{\{R_n^1,R_n^2,\ldots,R_n^m\}\rightarrow R_{n+1}}.
\]

The lower-level members:

- do not need to be identical;
- do not need to duplicate first;
- can have different roles and internal modes;
- remain internally active after the higher-level structure forms.

The higher level introduces new collective constraints and a new collective mode structure while containing the lower levels.

## 6. Variation

Different counts, arrangements, compositions, orientations, connections, phases, and environments may create different higher-level resonant geometries from the same lower-level building blocks.

\[
\boxed{\text{same or related lower units}+\text{different organization}\rightarrow\text{different }R_{n+1}}.
\]

Variation is therefore fully compatible with the core and requires no new principle.

## 7. Scale

A **scale** is a level at which a collective resonant geometry can function as an effective unit in further interactions.

Different scales may have different:

- characteristic sizes,
- characteristic times/frequencies,
- dominant interactions,
- effective mechanisms,
- compositions and geometries.

RRG does **not** require the same microscopic mechanism or identical equation at every scale.

## 8. Recursion

The core recursive claim is structural:

\[
\boxed{\{R_n^i\}\rightarrow R_{n+1}\rightarrow R_{n+2}\rightarrow\cdots}.
\]

At every level the locked relation remains:

\[
\boxed{R_n=(G_n,M_n),\qquad G_n\leftrightarrow M_n}.
\]

The mechanisms implementing the relation may change with scale.

## 9. Replication / recurrence

Replication, duplication, autocatalysis, reproduction, aggregation, differentiation, self-assembly, and symmetry breaking are **possible mechanisms of higher-level formation or propagation**, not mandatory steps in the core recursion.

RRG never requires:

\[
A\rightarrow A+A\rightarrow B
\]

at every level.

Biological replication is therefore an example, not the definition of recursion.

## 10. Interaction / force status

The following is **NOT locked as established fact**:

> known forces are identical to resonant frequencies or correspond one-to-one with scales.

The locked core only says that interactions occur within and between resonant geometries and can participate in forming higher-level geometries.

The stronger claim that gravity, electromagnetism, weak, and strong interactions are scale-dependent manifestations of deeper resonant geometry is an **RRG extension to be proven**, not a definition.

## 11. Background / possibility-space status

The idea that global cosmological/environmental conditions change which resonant geometries are accessible is an **extension compatible with the core**, not part of the minimal definition.

## 12. What counts as contradiction

An example does **not** contradict RRG merely because:

- the components are different;
- the higher level does not reproduce itself;
- the structure is short-lived;
- the mechanism differs from another scale;
- the system is stationary rather than visibly oscillating;
- lower-level units differentiate into different functions;
- the higher-level interaction differs from the lower-level interaction.

A genuine contradiction must show that a claimed RRG object cannot consistently be represented by the locked relation \(R=(G,M)\), or that the proposed recursive higher-level organization cannot be expressed without violating one of the locked definitions.

## 13. Version rule

This file cannot be changed silently.

Any proposed core change requires all of the following:

1. **Exact current statement** that allegedly fails.
2. **Concrete counterexample** that cannot be represented under that statement.
3. **External evidence or derivation** supporting the counterexample.
4. **Proof that an extension is insufficient** and the definition itself must change.
5. **Minimal proposed wording change.**
6. **Impact analysis** showing every previous RRG claim affected by the change.
7. **Explicit version bump and approval.**

Until all seven are present, the locked definition remains authoritative.

This is the definition authority for RRG. Geometry and full temporal mode structure describe one organized system. Stability means their self-consistent closure during an interval; it does not require permanence. Different parts, mechanisms and equations may occur at different scales. Force unification and background selection remain extensions.

For a simpler introduction, read [Start](/start/). The [change-control protocol](/changes/) states how a proposed contradiction must be handled.
